title: Handling a complaint
lede: These five steps are shuffled. Put them in the order you would use them with an unhappy customer.
intent: Learners can carry out the steps of handling a customer complaint in an order that resolves it rather than escalating it.
goal: handle a customer complaint in an order that settles it rather than escalating it.
prompt: In what order should you handle a customer complaint?

items.label: Listen without interrupting
items.why: People need to be heard before they can hear you. Jumping in with a fix usually makes it take longer.

items.label: Acknowledge it and apologise for the experience
items.why: Apologising for how it felt is not admitting fault. It puts you on their side of the problem.

items.label: Ask what would put it right
items.why: The fix you assume they want is often not the one they do.

items.label: Agree what you will do, and by when
items.why: A specific action and a time is what turns an apology into a plan.

items.label: Follow up afterwards
items.why: Checking back is what customers remember, and it catches the fixes that did not work.

sources.label: Steps written for this activity
sources.note: Check against your workplace's complaints procedure.
